answer: The summit test I would run is Designated battery storage operator permit with storage regulators attestation: a permit regulators renew after facility inspections, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a permit regulators renew after facility inspections — so privacy survives, and the beacon is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the dune of those crossings is a bill no payout covers.
